Sereact robots enter live Zalando returns operations in Germany and Poland

Cortex-powered dual-arm systems are operating with CEVA in Greven and Świebodzin under a RaaS model, handling unpredictable fashion returns.

CEVA Logistics ↗7 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 2

Two operational sites

On October 7, Sereact, Zalando and CEVA Logistics announced that dual-arm robots had entered live operations at Greven in Germany and Świebodzin in Poland. These sites are the first operational step in a broader European returns initiative. The development is a production deployment, following Zalando’s participation as a strategic investor in Sereact’s Series B in July.

Handling unfamiliar returns

Fashion returns often arrive crumpled or poorly packed, making fixed picking sequences difficult to apply. According to the partners, Cortex identifies, grasps and sorts unfamiliar objects without training separately for each article or relying on a predefined SKU set. The focus is adapting manipulation to the condition of each incoming item, rather than assuming identical presentation.

Service model and evidence limits

The deployment uses Robotics-as-a-Service, with the aim of reducing repetitive handling and physical strain. Employees remain responsible for station supervision, exceptions and quality control. The announcement does not provide robot counts, hourly throughput or independently measured error rates, so it does not establish a quantified cost saving or readiness for every warehouse environment.
